modules.brief: Read, write, edit and list the files of the workspace.
modules.detail:
Reading is the cheap direction of this sandbox and writing is the expensive one, so a program that reads a dozen files to decide what to change is well shaped, while one that rewrites forty large files in a single turn will exhaust its fuel budget.

Nothing here places anything in the agent's context window. `Views.OpenFile` is the call that does.

modules.brief: Run shell commands in the workspace.
modules.detail: One call, and the way a program reaches everything gg has no tool for: a build, a test run, `git`, `curl`, a package manager. The workspace is the working directory.

modules.brief: The epic and issue board, on which work is decomposed into dispatchable units.
modules.detail: An issue is heavyweight and self-contained: it says what is in scope, what is not, and how it will be judged done, and gg dispatches it to the agent it names. That is what makes it different from a task, which is a note an agent keeps for itself.

modules.brief: A private task list, held as a graph with blocker edges.
modules.detail: Small units of the agent's own work. Nobody dispatches from it — `Board` is where other agents pick work up.

modules.brief: Durable memories, which survive a context compaction.
modules.detail:
A run picks one of three memory strategies and binds only that strategy's calls: the scratchpad's `Memories.WriteMemory` and `Memories.UpdateMemory`, or the file-shaped `Memories.CreateMemory`, `Memories.ReadMemory` and `Memories.EditMemory` — plus `Memories.SearchMemories` where there is no pinned index. `Memories.DeleteMemory` is bound under all three, the system prompt says which strategy is in force, and `Memories.List` is the directory of what was really bound.

A memory may carry `code`, which is a module in this language bound at `lib.<name>` in every later program — a helper written once. It costs no context window and is never shown back.

modules.brief: Put a file, a computed value or a function's documentation into the context window.
modules.detail:
A program's own output goes nowhere the model can read it. A view is how a program puts something in front of the model that wrote it: one attributable item in the next prompt, closeable once it has been read.

There are three kinds and the list is closed: a file, a computed string, and one function's documentation. A picture is not a fourth kind — it is a file view of an image file, and the view carries the picture.

modules.brief: Reclaim room in the agent's own context window.
modules.detail: Four calls, in the order a full window wants them: drop file views that are done with, move whole turns into the archive, search the archive for what was moved, and — when none of that is enough — compact.

modules.brief: Delegate work to child agents, and hand this session on to another agent.
modules.detail: A child runs in parallel with its own window and its own model. It sees the brief it was given and nothing of the conversation that produced it, so a brief has to be self-contained — which is also why an issue, whose scope is written down, makes a better one than a sentence.

modules.brief: Read the authored skills this run offers.
modules.detail: A skill is a procedure somebody wrote down. The ones a run offers are named in the system prompt, and reading one pins it into the session permanently.

modules.brief: Fetch a program already run, and hand a patched copy back to be run.
modules.detail: Under responses-as-code a whole turn is a program, so a trivial mistake in a long one costs the whole program again. gg keeps the source of every program it ran: fetch one, patch it with ordinary string work, and hand it back.

modules.brief: End the session, with a summary or with a reviewer's verdict.
modules.detail: Under responses-as-code every turn is a program, so there is no prose turn that could mean the work is done. These calls mean it, and nothing else does. Which of them an agent has is decided by its role: an agent doing work ends with `Session.Finish`, and a reviewer returns a verdict with `Session.Approve` or `Session.RequestChanges`.

modules.brief: The types and the failure vocabulary every other module's signatures name.
modules.detail: They are declared directly in `namespace Gg`, which the SDK brings into every program's scope, so `ToolException` and `FunctionSummary` are written without a module prefix.

meta.name: List
meta.doc:
List the functions this module offers, each with a one-line summary.

Only the functions this run actually bound are returned, so the directory never names a call a program cannot make. One function's full signature, argument descriptions and types are opened as a view with `Views.OpenDocsView`.

Returns: the functions this module really bound, each with its one-line summary.

functions.name: CreateIssue
functions.brief: Create a self-contained, dispatchable issue, and get back the id the board gave it.
functions.detail:
The three scope arguments are what makes an issue dispatchable: the agent that picks it up sees them and nothing of the conversation that produced them, so anything it needs has to be in them.

```csharp
var created = Board.CreateIssue(
    title: "port the fixtures to the new schema",
    inScope: "everything under tests/fixtures",
    outOfScope: "the schema itself, which is already agreed",
    completionCriteria: "cargo nextest run --workspace passes",
    agent: "worker",
    epicId: "AUTH");
```

Returns: the id the board assigned, and how full the board now is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a blank field or an agent outside the spawnable set, `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an epic or blocker the board does not hold, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the issue cap.

functions.name: WaitForIssue
functions.brief: Register a wait on an issue, and get back an acknowledgement.
functions.detail:
It does not block inside the program: it records the wait and returns at once, so the rest of the program still runs. Once the program has ended the run suspends — freeing this agent's slot for others — until the issue is terminal, and then resumes with which way it went.

The issue an agent was assigned to implement is not one it may wait on.

Returns: an acknowledgement that the wait is registered.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a blank id, or for the issue this agent was itself assigned, `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an id the board does not hold, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when the run has no board.

parameters.doc: The issue to wait on.

functions.name: OpenFile
functions.brief: Read a file and show it in the context window.
functions.detail:
The read's result comes back exactly as `Files.ReadFile` returns it, and the file is added to the window as its own item. The separation is the point: `Files.ReadFile` gets bytes for the program, this shows a file to the model, and a program that reads forty files to grep them still adds nothing to the window.

The key is the path and the region together, so two pages of one file are two views and coexist. Opening the same page again replaces it rather than piling up a duplicate.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a missing path, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an offset past the end of the file.

signatures.signature: OpenFile(string path, uint? offset = null, uint? limit = null) -> Files.FileRead

parameters.name: path
parameters.doc: The file to read and show, relative to the workspace or absolute.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.doc: The 1-based first line. Left out, the whole file is shown.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.doc: How many lines. Left out, the view runs to the end.

functions.name: OpenText
functions.brief: Show a computed value in the context window, under a label.

parameters.name: label
parameters.doc: What to file it under. It is also what `Views.Close` takes, so an empty label is refused: a view with no selector could never be closed or replaced.

parameters.name: body
parameters.doc: The text to show. Empty is allowed, and is how a program says that something it was showing is now empty.

functions.name: OpenDocsView
functions.brief: Show the full documentation for one function in the context window.
functions.detail:
Its signature, its description, what each argument takes, and the declarations of any types it refers to that the session has not already been shown. It is a view rather than a return value: the documentation arrives in the next prompt, under a `Documentation` heading, and closes like anything else.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a name no function on this surface has.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The name a program calls the function by — `ReadFile`, `CreateIssue`, `Finish`. Searching the documentation is what says which names exist.

functions.detail: For a file, every page of that path closes. Closing a selector that is not open returns zero rather than failing.

parameters.name: selector

functions.brief: List what is open in the context window right now.

The files on disk are untouched; only the views of them go.

functions.name: ArchiveThread
functions.brief: Move whole turns out of the window, named by the turn numbers on each result.
functions.detail:
Ranges are inclusive and may overlap. The agent's own messages in an archived turn are dropped; the results are kept and stay searchable with `Context.SearchArchive`.

Returns: what was actually freed.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty list, too many spans at once, or a span that ends before it starts.

parameters.name: ranges
parameters.doc: The spans of turns to archive. Each is inclusive at both ends, and a span whose ends are equal archives one turn.

functions.name: SearchArchive
functions.brief: Search everything archived so far, case-insensitively, by substring.
functions.detail:
At most eight hits, most recent first. A search that matched nothing is an empty `Context.ArchiveSearch.Hits`; a search with nothing to look in says so through `Context.ArchiveSearch.ArchiveEmpty`, which is a different fact.

Returns: whether there was an archive at all, and what matched.

parameters.name: query
parameters.doc: The substring to look for.

functions.name: Compact
functions.brief: Compact the window: gg drops the detailed thread and restarts it from a summary.
functions.detail:
It is registered rather than performed: the call validates and returns, the program carries on, and gg rewrites the window once the program has ended — a context reset has no shape inside the program whose context it resets. A second call simply replaces the request.

Skills, memories and the task list are kept regardless. gg asks for this call when the window is full and refuses every other call until it is made, so it is available at all times.

signatures.signature: Compact(string summary, params string[] files) -> void

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: Everything the next window has to start from: what is being done, what has been found, and what is left.

parameters.name: files
parameters.doc: Workspace paths to read freshly into the new window.

functions.name: SpawnSubagent
functions.brief: Delegate scoped work to a child agent, and get its handle back immediately.
functions.detail:
The child runs in parallel and nothing here waits for it; `Delegation.WaitForSubagents` collects it later.

```csharp
var child = Delegation.SpawnSubagent("worker", Delegation.Brief.Issue("AUTH-1"));
var results = Delegation.WaitForSubagents(child.Id);
```

Returns: the child's handle — its id, the profile it runs as, and the model bound to it.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an agent outside the spawnable set, and `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap.

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to run the child as, drawn from the spawnable set the system prompt lists. It selects the child's model, tools and instructions.

parameters.name: task
parameters.doc: What the child should do: a written prompt, or a board issue whose scope becomes the brief.

functions.name: WaitForSubagents
functions.brief: Wait for every outstanding child, and collect their results.
functions.detail:
This blocks while it waits, and the run's wall-clock budget keeps running while it does, so one wait for many children costs far less than one wait per child.

Returns: one result per child, in the order they were collected.

`WaitForSubagents(params string[] ids)` — Wait for the named children, and collect their results.

Returns: one result per named child, in the order they were collected.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an id this agent never spawned.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.doc: The child ids to wait for, as `Delegation.SpawnSubagent` handed them back.

functions.name: SendMessage
functions.brief: Deliver a message to a running child's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail: Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for an unknown child, and `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for one that has already returned.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.doc: The child to write to.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to tell it.

functions.name: TransitionState
functions.brief: Move the process this agent runs inside on to another of its states.
functions.detail:
It is registered rather than performed: the call validates the target against the reachable states, returns, and the program carries on to its end; the transition happens after that. Replacing the agent, and its window, while its own program is still running would pull every remaining call out from under it.

The first declaration stands and a second is refused, because a silently replaced successor is a change nobody can see. It is bound only where a state machine is driving the agent and the current state has somewhere to go.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` names an unreachable state, `ToolErrorCode.Refused` means a succession was already declared this turn, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` means no machine is driving this agent.

signatures.signature: TransitionState(string state, string? note = null) -> void

parameters.name: state
parameters.doc: The state to move to, named the way an agent to spawn is named.

parameters.name: note
parameters.doc: The opening message the next state's agent sees.

functions.name: Exec
functions.brief: Continue this session as a different agent.
functions.detail:
The successor takes over from the next turn with its own model, tools and instructions, keeping every capability the two share — the whole conversation above all. Registered exactly as `Delegation.TransitionState` is, and for the same reason.

The first declaration of a succession stands, so an `Exec` after a `Delegation.TransitionState`, or a second `Exec`, is refused.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` names an agent outside that set, `ToolErrorCode.Refused` means a succession was already declared this turn, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` means this agent is running inside a machine, which leaves by `Delegation.TransitionState` instead.

signatures.signature: Exec(string agent, string? prompt = null) -> void

parameters.name: agent
parameters.doc: The agent to become, drawn from the set this agent may become.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: The opening message it sees.

functions.name: Fork
functions.brief: Run a copy of this agent, in parallel, on something it will not do itself.
functions.detail:
The copy has this agent's model, its tools and a private copy of its whole conversation, so the prompt is the difference rather than a briefing.

Its handle comes back immediately, and the copy itself starts once this turn's results are recorded — the conversation it inherits has to be a complete one — so `Delegation.WaitForSubagents` can only collect it on a later turn.

Returns: the copy's handle.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a blank prompt, `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` at the delegation depth cap, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` with no delegation runtime to collect the copy with.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.doc: What this copy is to do differently.

functions.name: ReadSkill
functions.brief: Read an authored skill by name, front matter stripped.
functions.detail:
The skill is also pinned permanently into the session's context, so it survives a compaction and never has to be read twice. A skill that carries code binds that code at `lib.<name>` for every later program.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` for a name this run has no skill under.

parameters.name: name
parameters.doc: The skill's name, exactly as the system prompt lists it. An unknown one comes back with the full list of the skills this run has.

functions.name: History
functions.brief: List the programs this session has run, oldest first.
functions.detail:
Each entry carries the shape of a program rather than its source: a directory that inlined sixty lines per entry would put the whole session back into the one place that exists to avoid re-reading it. It is empty before the first program has been recorded.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when this agent keeps no program library.

functions.name: Get
functions.brief: Fetch the exact source of one program, as it was run.
functions.detail:
As it was run is the contract that matters: where a turn's program was itself handed over by an earlier one, what is kept is the program that executed rather than the few lines that asked for it. So fetching, patching and re-running composes.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.NotFound` — naming the turns that are held — for a turn that ran no program, or one the library's retention has already dropped, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when this agent keeps no program library.

parameters.name: turn
parameters.doc: The turn to fetch, as `Programs.ProgramSummary.Turn` reports it. Left out, the most recent one is returned.

functions.name: Rerun
functions.brief: Hand gg a program to run in place of this one.
functions.detail:
It is registered rather than performed. The call returns and the rest of the program still runs; only once it has ended does gg compile and run what was handed over. Everything the registering program did stands — its calls, its views — and the program that runs next sees exactly the world it left behind.

```csharp
var previous = Programs.Get();
Programs.Rerun(previous.Replace("--release", "--debug"));
```

The first call stands and a second is refused, because a silently replaced program is a change nobody can see. The request is revoked if the program then fails, on the same rule an ending is.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for a blank source, `ToolErrorCode.Refused` for a second call in one turn, and `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when this agent keeps no program library.

parameters.name: source
parameters.doc: The program to run instead. Blank is refused.

functions.name: Finish
functions.brief: Declare the work complete.
functions.detail:
It sets a flag on gg's side and returns normally. It does not stop the program, it throws nothing, and nothing after it is refused: gg reads the flag once the program has ended, and a second call simply replaces the declaration.

The flag is revoked if the program then fails — an uncaught exception, or a sandbox ceiling stopping it. A program that did not run to its end did not run the checks its summary claims, so the session carries on and the ending is reported as cancelled.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when the agent's role does not end this way, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty summary.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.doc: The last word: for a root agent the run's final text, for a child its return value to whoever asked for the work. It must not be empty.

functions.name: Approve
functions.brief: Declare the work under review acceptable.
functions.detail:
It takes nothing, deliberately: an approval carries no further obligation, and a shape that demanded prose would be a shape gg had to read back. It ends the session under the same rules `Session.Finish` does, and is revoked the same way.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when the agent's role returns no verdict.

functions.name: RequestChanges
functions.brief: Declare the work unacceptable, listing every change it needs.
functions.detail:
A rejection with nothing to act on leaves the agent that has to fix the work no work to do, which is why the empty case is refused rather than represented. It ends the session under the same rules `Session.Finish` does.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Unavailable` when the agent's role returns no verdict, and `ToolErrorCode.InvalidArgument` for an empty list or a blank entry.

parameters.name: items
parameters.doc: One entry per change, each saying what is wrong and what to change. At least one, and none of them blank.

functions.name: Send
functions.brief: Deliver a message to this child's inbox, which it reads at its next turn.
functions.detail:
`Delegation.SendMessage` with the id already supplied, for the common case where the handle is in hand.

Throws `ToolException`: `ToolErrorCode.Conflict` for a child that has already returned.

parameters.name: message
parameters.doc: What to tell it.

types.name: ToolErrorCode
types.declaration: enum ToolErrorCode { InvalidArgument, NotFound, Conflict, Refused, Unavailable, LimitExceeded, IOError, Other }
types.brief: Why a gg call failed, in the vocabulary a `catch` branches on.
types.detail: A code is never derived from the wording of a message: every gg tool classifies its own failures where it raises them, and this is that classification. Branching on it is stable in a way that branching on `System.Exception.Message` is not.

members.brief: The arguments were malformed, ill-typed, or out of range.

members.name: NotFound
members.brief: The named file, skill, memory, task, epic, issue, subagent or program is not there.

members.name: Conflict
members.brief: Well-formed, and in conflict with how things stand.
members.detail: An ambiguous edit, a dependency cycle, a duplicate id, a child agent that has already returned.

members.name: Refused
members.brief: gg refused the call because of a rule about the agent's own state.
members.detail: A read-only memory, a call a pending compaction does not admit, a second succession in one turn, or a hook that blocked it. A ceiling that was reached is `ToolErrorCode.LimitExceeded` instead.

members.name: Unavailable
members.brief: The call exists and this run does not offer it to this agent.
members.detail: A tool outside the run's capability set, an ending the agent's role does not declare, or a program library this agent does not keep. The recovery is to stop asking for it.

members.name: LimitExceeded
members.brief: A gg-side ceiling was reached.
members.detail: A shell timeout, a memory, task or board cap, the delegation depth cap, a view cap a program spends, or the run's wall-clock budget running out mid-program.

members.name: IOError
members.brief: The underlying input, output or process failed.

members.name: Other
members.brief: The failure was not classified.
members.detail: No tool produces it; it is reserved for outcomes raised outside a tool implementation.
